runs.text:
Take a look at a tangled bank sometime. You'll see plants of every kind, birds singing in the bushes, insects darting around, and worms working through the damp soil. Here's the interesting part: these complex, wildly different living things, all depending on each other in tangled ways, came from laws that are still at work around us right now.

What are those laws? Growth and reproduction. Inheritance, which comes bundled with reproduction. Variability, driven by how living things react to their surroundings and by use and disuse. And a rate of increase so high it forces a struggle for life — which leads to natural selection, which in turn drives character to diverge and weaker forms to die out.

So here's the payoff: out of nature's struggle, out of famine and death, comes the thing we find most awe-inspiring — the higher animals. That's the direct result.

And there's something grand in that. Picture life's many powers breathed into just a few forms, maybe even one. Then picture this planet spinning on through time, bound by nothing more than the fixed law of gravity — and from that simple start, endless forms, each more beautiful and wonderful than the last, have evolved, and are evolving still.
